clue.text: Flight controller delights parasite

parts.note: delights as a plural noun means joys
a tick is a blood-sucking parasite

explanation.surface: Someone at the controls of a plane is thrilled by a bloodsucker.
explanation.definitionFit: A joystick is the control lever a pilot uses to steer an aircraft.

clue.text: Miscellaneous collection for two biblical characters

parts.note: Job is the long-suffering figure of the Old Testament book of that name
Lot is Abraham's nephew in Genesis

explanation.surface: A mixed bag set aside for two figures from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: A JOB LOT is an auction term for a mixed batch of goods sold together.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction lot of assorted items sold as one is called this.

clue.text: Singular chest, many sailors

indicators.note: singular in the sense of odd or peculiar tells us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: One chest of belongings shared among a crowd of seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' looks like a grammar word set against 'many'; it is the anagram signal on CHEST and MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Yachtsmen are people who sail yachts, so they are a kind of sailor.

clue.text: Silent American leaving ancient historian

indicators.note: leaving means the American abbreviation departs from the historian's name

parts.note: Tacitus was a Roman historian of the first century

explanation.surface: A quiet American walks away from a classical scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes US from the end of TACITUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken, understood without words being said.

clue.text: Charles Stuart's head is taken from body?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so take the opening of Stuart's

explanation.surface: A grim reference to the beheading of the Stuart king Charles I.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Charles I losing his head; in fact 'head' only picks the S from Stuart.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the framework or body of a vehicle; the question mark admits the looseness.

clue.text: Hunter taking one drink after another

definitions.meaning: a short drink taken straight after another, such as a beer after a whisky

explanation.surface: A huntsman knocking back drink after drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the word: a pursuer in a hunt, and a follow-up drink taken after a spirit.

clue.text: Novelist or musician getting fish to rise

parts.note: a harper is someone who plays the harp

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A writer, or perhaps a harpist, getting a fish to take the bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns EEL into LEE. Harper Lee wrote To Kill a Mockingbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Harper Lee was the American author of the novel To Kill a Mockingbird.

clue.text: He's very lecherous one day a year

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday

explanation.surface: A man who lets himself go just once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a lustful woodland creature of Greek myth, hence a lecherous man.

clue.text: Wealthy Scottish man comes to bad end somewhere in Yorkshire or Surrey

parts.note: wealthy means rich
mon is a Scots form of man

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here the last of bad

explanation.surface: A rich Scot comes to grief somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: There are towns called Richmond in both North Yorkshire and Surrey (now in Greater London).
explanation.definitionFit: Richmond is the name of a town in North Yorkshire and of one in Surrey.

clue.text: Second bird with sauce

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a chat is a small songbird such as the stonechat

explanation.surface: A second helping of bird served with gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' is not gravy but cheek, impudent talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce in the sense of cheek or impudence matches cheeky answering back.

clue.text: Lorry going round central sea

indicators.note: going round means the lorry word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a British term for a large truck
C is an abbreviation for central, as in London postcodes such as WC (West Central)

explanation.surface: A truck circling the middle of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: An ARTIC is British slang for an articulated lorry (a semi-trailer truck).
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic is the ocean, and sea, around the North Pole.

clue.text: As far as possible, providing a little fruit

indicators.note: providing means the run of words supplies the answer from within

explanation.surface: Doing as much as one can, on condition of getting some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'providing' looks like 'on condition that'; it means the words supply the letters, inside fAR AS Possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasp is a short informal name for raspberry, so a clipped bit of the fruit's name.

clue.text: Eight players given a month on eight sides

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters, here of eight

explanation.surface: Eight musicians hired for a month on an eight-sided stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight performers.

clue.text: Caught with odd instrument

parts.note: caught means snared, trapped
rum is British informal for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone trapped with a strange musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM as an adjective meaning odd is British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument with wires across its lower skin.

clue.text: Friends going about in city — all French

indicators.note: going about means the friends word wraps around the next piece

parts.note: amis is French for friends
en is French for in

explanation.surface: French friends wander about a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all French' tells you both AMIS and EN are French words.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a city in northern France.

clue.text: Form solid pile in solid form

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it, so the letters are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: Building a pile into a solid shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' at the start is the anagram signal; the definition is 'solid form' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipsoid is a three-dimensional shape whose cross-sections are ellipses.

clue.text: Fifty per cent of ladies in distress required a knight-errant

indicators.note: in means the half word goes inside the distress word

parts.note: distress means pain

indicators.note: fifty per cent of a six-letter word is its first three letters

explanation.surface: Damsels in distress needing a knight to rescue them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifty per cent of' takes LAD, the first half of LADIES, which goes 'in' PAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin was one of Charlemagne's champions, hence a heroic wandering knight.

clue.text: Bird found on river? Only fish

parts.note: a dove is a bird
sole means only

explanation.surface: A bird spotted by a river is the only fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover sole is a flatfish prized as food.

clue.text: One not employed in mine — girl not needing a reminder

indicators.note: not employed in means the one is left out of the word mine

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: not needing means the a is dropped from the girl's name

parts.note: Monica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An idle miner and a girl who never needs reminding.
explanation.walkthrough: MINE less I gives MNE; MONICA less A gives MONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A mnemonic is a memory aid, a device that jogs recall.

clue.text: Negative puzzle?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., that is not positive, the word playfully means negative

explanation.surface: A puzzle that gives a negative result.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus is to baffle; split as non-plus it whimsically suggests minus, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Loafer, possibly, to work as a farrier

definitions.meaning: a loafer is a type of slip-on footwear, given as an example
a farrier fits iron plates to horses' hooves

explanation.surface: A layabout who might work as a blacksmith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loafer' looks like an idler but is a slip-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer is one kind of footwear, and fitting horses' hooves with iron is what a farrier does.

clue.text: Split stick

definitions.meaning: to divide by a blow, as with a chopper

explanation.surface: A broken piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is its own opposite: it means both to divide apart and to cling closely.

clue.text: Herb and Sonny's former partner versus the Italian

parts.note: Cher sang with her husband Sonny Bono as Sonny and Cher
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Herb competing against an Italian, with a pop singer's ex involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Chervil is a parsley-like culinary herb.

clue.text: Coy about a gee-gee being poorly groomed

indicators.note: about means the coy word goes around the rest

parts.note: coy means shy
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse, abbreviated GG

explanation.surface: A bashful rider standing by an untidy horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaggy means having long unkempt hair, so badly groomed.

clue.text: Eh? Map gone astray? For crying out loud!

indicators.note: astray means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lost traveller exclaims in frustration that the map has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For crying out loud!' sounds like an exclamation; it defines something used for shouting loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaphone is a cone used to amplify the voice when calling out.

clue.text: Associate harmoniously with board

definitions.meaning: to have a friendly relationship with someone
to climb aboard a bus or train

explanation.surface: Getting along well with the board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Two phrasal senses: rubbing along well with people, and climbing onto a vehicle.

clue.text: Church on high ground that provides illumination

indicators.note: on means the church abbreviation comes after the high ground in an across entry

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: A church on a hilltop acting as a beacon.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hilltop, a word common in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable light, a flashlight in British usage.

clue.text: Unaffected by flipping doctrine

indicators.note: unaffected by flipping means the word reads the same backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A principle that does not change when turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held by a group.

clue.text: Thought about it in time?

indicators.note: in means the turned word goes inside the time

parts.note: noon is a time of day

indicators.note: about means the word it is turned round

explanation.surface: Wondering whether it was done on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns IT into TI, which goes 'in' NOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or thought.

clue.text: Steven, no saint, possibly lied in church service

indicators.note: no means the saint abbreviation is removed from the name

parts.note: a lied is a German art song, so an example of a song

explanation.surface: A churchgoer named Steven, no saint, may have told untruths in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lied' looks like told a lie; it is the German word for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening prayer service of the Anglican church.

clue.text: Country woman is able to lead

indicators.note: to lead means the is-able word goes in front

parts.note: can means is able
Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A capable woman put in charge of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a North American nation.

clue.text: Fly around, say, like a butterfly?

definitions.text: Fly around, say, like a butterfly?

parts.words: Fly around, say, like a butterfly?
parts.note: the whole clue describes the flitting, wavering motion of a butterfly's wings, playing on the butter in butterfly

explanation.surface: Darting about in the way a butterfly does.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluttery means given to rapid, flapping movement, the way a butterfly moves.
